channel.title: Daily Perspective
channel.description: A daily digest of tech, world, economy and perspective.

item.title: Friday, November 13, 2026
item.description: Behind every outage, outbreak, or market dip are people improvising without power, medicine, or certainty—whose resilience rarely makes the headline. Whose daily disruption might you be overlooking?

item.title: Thursday, November 12, 2026
item.description: When infrastructure fails—whether a datacenter, a hospital, or a family budget—someone absorbs the shock quietly. Whose resilience are you relying on today without noticing?

item.title: Wednesday, November 11, 2026
item.description: Behind every funding round and policy debate are people displaced by storms, violence, or scarcity — whose daily survival doesn't pause for our markets or models. Whose reality are you overlooking today?

item.title: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
item.description: Behind each fiber-optic cable, inflation statistic, and ceasefire violation is someone's daily survival. What would today's headlines look like if written by the people living inside them, not observing from outside?

item.title: Monday, November 9, 2026
item.description: While markets fixate on one CEO's scandal, families in Gaza, Ukraine, and Kenya face winter with no safety net at all—whose crisis actually deserves today's attention, and whose is just noise?

item.title: Sunday, November 8, 2026
item.description: Export controls, research dissolutions, self-improving models—each sounds abstract until you ask who decides, and who's left out. Whose fate depends today on a border, a deportation list, a policy memo they'll never see?

item.title: Saturday, November 7, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center debate and market jitter are people—displaced families rebuilding in floodwaters, aid workers stretched thin. Progress means little if it doesn't ask: whose daily reality are we actually improving?

item.title: Friday, November 6, 2026
item.description: Behind every AI headline is a chip worker on strike, a refugee facing harsher climate, a family losing aid funding. Whose labor or safety are you not seeing when you read about progress today?

item.title: Thursday, November 5, 2026
item.description: Behind every outage, sentence, or algorithm lies someone's labor or liberty—the ranch host, the striking worker, the jailed activist. Whose unseen effort or risk makes your convenience possible today?

item.title: Wednesday, November 4, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center protest, crypto heist, and ceasefire headline are people trying to protect something fragile—home, savings, safety. What would you need before trusting the systems making decisions over your life?

item.title: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
item.description: Behind every headline—a dismantled botnet, a displacement camp, a tax debate—is someone's daily life upended or steadied. What would today's news look like if you had to live inside its consequences?

item.title: Monday, November 2, 2026
item.description: Behind every layoff number, scraped dataset, or ceasefire violation is someone whose daily life just changed. What would today's headlines feel like if they were about your job, your city, your family?

item.title: Sunday, November 1, 2026
item.description: When headlines reduce distant lives to statistics—civilian deaths, outbreak counts, detention records—pause: each number is someone's whole world ending or barely holding on. Whose perspective haven't you imagined today?

item.title: Saturday, October 31, 2026
item.description: Behind every AI spending chart and crypto hack is a cascade reaching real paychecks and safety; behind every ceasefire's fine print are people simply trying to walk home unharmed. Whose daily calculus are you overlooking today?

item.title: Friday, October 30, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center, evacuation order, and layoff memo is someone whose daily life just shifted. What would today's headlines feel like if you were the one living inside them, not reading about them?

item.title: Thursday, October 29, 2026
item.description: Behind every headline—AI job loss, Gaza's hunger, a budget's fine print—is someone's ordinary day upended. What would you need others to understand if it were yours?

item.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
item.description: Behind each headline—AI lawsuits, cyber threats, ceasefires, budgets—are people making sense of uncertainty. Whose perspective haven't you considered today, and what might they need you to understand?

item.title: Tuesday, October 27, 2026
item.description: Behind every infrastructure cost and buyout headline is someone recalculating their life. Can you hold the systemic story and the individual one at the same time, without letting either erase the other?

item.title: Monday, October 26, 2026
item.description: Behind every layoff statistic and IPO headline is a person recalculating their life—just as behind every conflict report is someone rebuilding theirs. Whose perspective are you missing today?

item.title: Sunday, October 25, 2026
item.description: Before reacting to today's headlines, ask: whose daily survival is reduced to a data point here—and what would the story look like told from inside their life, not above it?

item.title: Saturday, October 24, 2026
item.description: Behind every data policy and border tariff is someone's daily life being quietly reshaped—whose perspective are you missing when a headline feels abstract rather than personal?

item.title: Friday, October 23, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center's power bill and every ceasefire rumor is someone whose daily life hangs on decisions made far away. Whose perspective are you missing today?

item.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center's water use, every blocked port, every drone strike statistic, there's someone whose daily life just got harder. What would today's news look like written from their perspective instead of ours?

item.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026
item.description: Policy debates and inflation numbers are abstractions until you remember each one lands on someone harvesting olives, fleeing a drone, or counting grocery receipts—whose eyes would change how you read today's headlines?

item.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026
item.description: Behind every data point—displaced Yemenis, hungry families, AI-disrupted jobs—is someone navigating uncertainty you'll never face. What would change if policy debates started with their names, not statistics?

item.title: Monday, October 19, 2026
item.description: Behind every headline about AI governance or infrastructure failure are people who built something fragile by hand—much like the half-million in Gaza facing winter without food. Scale shifts; vulnerability doesn't.

item.title: Sunday, October 18, 2026
item.description: Behind today's headlines on surveillance, sanctions, and budgets are people adapting to forces beyond their control—whether a warehouse worker, a displaced family, or a miner. What would today's news look like through their eyes, not just the systems'?

item.title: Saturday, October 17, 2026
item.description: Sudan's famine and Ethiopia-Eritrea's tension get a fraction of the attention Ukraine or Gaza receive—worth asking why some suffering feels more visible to you than other suffering, and what that quiet hierarchy costs the people living it.

item.title: Friday, October 16, 2026
item.description: Behind every headline—olive groves destroyed, a collapsed school, a contested data policy—are people navigating systems built without them in mind. Whose perspective is missing from the story you just read?

item.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026
item.description: Behind every policy debate—AI hiring algorithms, inflation numbers, ceasefire terms—are people making impossible choices with incomplete information, much like the Afghan parents facing drought. What would you need to feel safe enough to hope?
